sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Streaming digital humans produce detailed video while continuing speech as new text arrives. High-resolution denoising is costly, and text updates can cause repeated or interrupted speech. We present TaoMate-HD, an autoregressive model for high-resolution audio-video streaming. For each short segment, or chunk, two denoising steps establish coarse video structure at low resolution. A final step refines the video to high resolution, with audio generated throughout the same trajectory. Each stage passes its audiovisual predictions to the same stage of the next chunk as history. Across text updates, the model retains this history to infer what has already been spoken. Continuation training utilizes asymmetric text conditioning, with separate text windows for generation and distillation. Experiments show a 1.6x speedup over direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Optimized stage-parallel deployment provides a further 1.9x overall speedup over serial progressive generation. Our continuation training reduces character error rate by 11.18 percentage points relative to the baseline. The model also supports hour-long audiovisual generation. Our project page is https://taoliveaigc.github.io/TaoMate-HD.

Each stage passes its audiovisual predictions to the same stage of the next chunk as history. Across text updates, the model retains this history to infer what has already been spoken. Experiments show 1.6 speedup over direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Optimized stage-parallel deployment provides further 1.9 overall speedup over serial progressive generation. Our continuation training reduces character error rate by 11.18 percentage points relative to the baseline. The model also supports hour-long audiovisual generation. sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Interactive digital humans need to sustain speech and visual motion as new dialogue arrives. Joint audio-video models generate both modalities from text [14]. Recent streaming systems extend this process over successive short segments, or chunks [57]. These streams must preserve fine details in faces, hands, and foreground objects while keeping speech continuous. Meeting both requirements is difficult: high-resolution synthesis is expensive, and text updates can disrupt ongoing speech. Direct high-resolution generation processes dense video-token grid at every denoising step. Even early steps use this grid when they mainly establish scene layout and motion. Few-step distillation reduces the number of steps [8, 9]. Progressive-resolution methods further reduce spatial computation by using coarser grids early in denoising [10, 11]. However, faster processing of one chunk does not remove the wait between chunks. If chunk needs the previous chunks final output as history, it must wait for all refinement to finish. Stage-parallel inference overlaps denoising across chunks [12], but requires usable audiovisual context before that final output. Speech continuity poses related challenge when text changes during generation. Streaming models retain audiovisual context across chunks [57]. To continue speech, they must relate incoming text to the words already spoken. Text-window boundaries need not coincide with sentence endings, so an update may arrive mid-sentence *Equal contribution. Corresponding author. Progressive audiovisual generation sustained over an hour. Top: MiniMax-H3 denoises high-resolution clips and passes frame to the next clip, while TaoMate uses few-step fixed-resolution generation with persistent audiovisual memory. TAOM AT E-HD refines each chunk through two low-resolution evaluations and one high-resolution evaluation, passing each stages audiovisual prediction to the next chunk. Retained history supports speech continuation as text windows advance. L/H denote low/high video grids. Bottom: full frames from two 60-minute, 1376 768 audiovisual streams at the labeled times (minutes:seconds). The sampled frames preserve character appearance and scene composition across the hour. and include words already spoken. Restarting from the first word repeats content, while stopping at the window boundary interrupts speech. The model therefore needs recent audio to distinguish spoken context from upcoming dialogue. We present TaoMate-HD, an autoregressive model for high-resolution audio-video streaming (Figure 1). Its central idea is to reuse audiovisual predictions before final spatial refinement is complete. Each chunk first undergoes two denoising steps at low resolution to establish coarse video structure. One final step refines the video to high resolution, while audio is generated throughout the joint trajectory. Each stage estimates clean audio and video without waiting for the remaining denoising steps. These estimates provide history for the same stage of the next chunk. The next chunk can thus begin coarse generation before the previous chunk finishes high-resolution refinement. When the text window changes, we retain the audiovisual history and use overlapping text to provide continuation context. The model infers speech progress from the retained audio, without an explicit text pointer or online speech recognizer. We train this behavior on the models own generated sequences, including text-window changes and speech completion. Training uses asymmetric text conditioning to separate generation from sequence-level supervision. The generator receives upcoming dialogue, while distillation uses the opening text context to evaluate the full audiovisual sequence. Experiments show that progressive generation is 1.60 faster than direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Compared with the baseline, our continuation training reduces character error rate from 30.75% to 19.57%. We also demonstrate hour-long audiovisual generation. Our contributions are threefold: progressive audio-video generator that concentrates denoising on coarse grid. Stage-local audiovisual history enables overlapping generation across chunks. Continuation training with asymmetric text conditioning and student-generated history to support speech across overlapping text windows. Hour-long high-resolution audiovisual demonstrations and quantitative comparisons of spatial efficiency, deployment throughput, and transcript accuracy. 2 TaoMate-HD

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Technical Report October 2026 Few-step autoregressive audio-video generation. Joint diffusion and flow models couple visual motion with speech and other acoustic content [14]. Progressive distillation, consistency training, and distribution matching reduce sampling to small number of evaluations [1316]. For streaming generation, these few-step trajectories must also learn to condition on previously generated content. CausVid uses distribution matching to distill bidirectional teacher into causal generator, with teacher ODE trajectories for initialization [8]. Self Forcing trains on student-generated histories and samples denoising exits for gradient computation [9]. Recent AV systems combine such rollouts with multimodal objectives and streaming inference [5, 1720]. LynnReal-Omni provides Standard and Flash joint-AV generators and extends generation through bounded latent history and boundary overlap [7]. We likewise train on student-generated histories, but allow the generators text window to advance while the distillation scores evaluate the sequence from its opening context. Progressive spatial computation. Few-step sampling still pays for dense grid at each evaluation. Progressive spatial methods reduce this cost by varying resolution along the trajectory. Matryoshka diffusion and pyramidal flow use multiple spatial scales within generation [10, 21]. PyramidalWan first adapts the original-architecture teacher to multiple resolutions through flow matching, then studies distribution matching with this teacher and refitted pyramidal teacher [11]. Its few-step schedule concentrates target-resolution computation in single evaluation. Spectral schedules and adaptive patch granularity likewise vary spatial computation with noise level [22, 23]. Video DeltaNet instead changes video-to-video attention through local Softmax, boundary anchors, and bidirectional linear memory, retaining Softmax interactions with text and audio [24]. Causal super-resolution methods such as Ultra Flash take another approach, refining the output of separate generator [25]. We change resolution within the joint audiovisual trajectory rather than after generation, and make the intermediate audiovisual predictions available as history for subsequent chunks. Temporal memory and denoising parallelism. Across chunks, efficiency also depends on when history becomes available. Long-video generators retain context through windows of cached features, recurrent state, selected history, or persistent anchors [2631]. TaoMate separates an immutable visual anchor and adaptive audiovisual memory from the active KV cache, using memory attention and reference-aware modulation for long-form consistency [6]. Its stage-parallel inference operates at fixed spatial resolution. Ripple also extends recurrent temporal state to joint audio-video generation [32]. Stage-parallel inference organizes chunks and denoising stages into an anti-diagonal pipeline and fuses context writing with the next chunks denoising [12]. The stage-specific history in that formulation is represented at the stages output noise level. We use this execution organization with paired clean audiovisual predictions on each stages native grid. The clean prediction provides common history representation even though the query noise level and spatial grid differ between stages.

sections.content: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive audio-video model that uses coarse-to-fine denoising and stage-local KV history to generate continuous stream (Figure 2). Each chunk develops on coarse video grid before high-resolution refinement, while intermediate audiovisual predictions provide context for subsequent chunks. Training on the models own rollouts with asymmetric text conditioning supports speech continuation as the dialogue advances. 3.1 Progressive generation Direct high-resolution generation repeats full-grid attention at every denoising step, including early steps that establish scene layout and large-scale motion. We therefore give each stage its own key/value (KV) history bank, built from the preceding chunks same-stage video and audio predictions. This encoding turns an intermediate endpoint estimate into reusable context without waiting for later denoising stages. The coarse-stage banks remain separate because they contain predictions at different refinement levels, while the final-stage bank stores the high-resolution endpoint. (3) These dependencies permit stage-parallel inference [12]: later chunks can occupy coarse stages while an earlier chunk undergoes final refinement. Each stage keeps its KV history local and passes current-chunk audiovisual latents downstream. Within text window, coarse stages fuse encoding of the preceding chunks clean estimate with denoising of the current noisy chunk [12]. causal mask lets the noisy chunk read that estimate and earlier history, while the context chunk reads prior history and itself. For long-stream inference, each bank retains the initial chunks video as visual anchor and the two most recent chunks paired video and audio. Initial audio remains available while it lies in this recent window. The fixed-capacity banks preserve appearance and recent speech context without growing with stream duration. KV and cached text projections are stored separately. text-window change refreshes the latter, leaving retained KV encoded under their original conditions. Before the switch, any pending clean prediction is committed at noise using the old window that generated it. Algorithm 1 summarizes this update for each stage. Algorithm 1 KV update at text-window boundary 1: Commit any pending clean estimate under 𝑐𝐺 old. 2: Retain initial-video KV and the two most recent AV chunks. 3: Activate 𝑐𝐺 new and refresh cached text projections. 4: Preserve retained KV and their temporal positions. 5: Denoise the next chunk with 𝑐𝐺 new and this history. Thus new text controls future synthesis without re-encoding the generated past. Spatial coordinates remain native to each grid, and temporal positions continue across windows. Training uses the same update order but retains the full causal prefix of its short rollouts. 3.3 Asymmetric distillation for continuation Speech continuation requires relating new dialogue to the retained audio history. We use overlapping text windows because updates can arrive mid-sentence. Let 𝐴 be earlier text, 𝐵 the shared span, and 𝐶 new dialogue. The generator moves from the initial window 𝑊1 = 𝐴 + 𝐵 to 𝑊2 = 𝐵 + 𝐶 while retaining history, using 𝐵 as context rather than restarting it. At inference, audio history and text indicate speech progress without ASR, text pointers, or alignment modules. We train this behavior on student-generated rollouts [9]. The student executes all 𝑁 stages, updates its own history banks, and switches text at sampled chunk boundary. To construct the windows, we extend source transcripts with same-topic speech while preserving the original wording, language, and speaker assignments. Source speaking rate maps nominal time intervals to character or word spans. The initial window 𝐴 + 𝐵 covers the entire nominal rollout horizon even when the switch occurs earlier. Distribution-matching distillation (DMD) supervises these rollouts by comparing frozen teacher score with learned score of the students distribution [15, 16]. The generator needs 𝑊2 to continue the next chunk, whereas both scores evaluate the concatenated sequence from its beginning. The learned fake score therefore retains 𝑊1: it includes the opening words absent from 𝑊2 and the extended dialogue conditioning the students rollout. The frozen real score instead uses the original source transcript prefix through the rollout duration. This ties the teacher 5 TaoMate-HD Technical Report October 2026 reference to the source segment, while the appended dialogue serves as generation lookahead. Scene descriptions, speaker attributes, and audiovisual alignment instructions are shared across all three roles during training. The generator uses 𝑊1 before the switch and 𝑊2 afterward, with ellipses marking omitted words: Generator (𝑊2) Fake (𝑊1) Real (source prefix) set of free templates you can download and use right away. These templates are designed to . . . this into my own post-processing workflow. . . . set of free templates you can download and use right away. These templates are designed this into my own post-processing workflow. . . . Ill even give you set Both scores receive the same audiovisual sequence, corruption noise, and noise levels, so their difference defines the DMD update at common noisy state. The fake score learns from detached student sequences by velocity regression with an independent noise draw. To supervise every refinement level, we sample one stage per rollout and concatenate its clean predictions across chunks. The selected stage is shared across chunks so the sequence has consistent refinement level. For coarse stage, bilinear interpolation enlarges the clean video latents to 𝐻, leaving time, channels, and audio unchanged. This gives both scores common high-resolution supervision canvas. The student continues to denoise on each stages native grid. Resizing the predicted clean video for scoring lets the high-resolution teacher supervise coarse stages without changing their computational resolution. All 𝑁 stages still execute for every chunk, irrespective of the stage selected for supervision. We first construct the rollout without gradients, then replay the selected evaluation one chunk at time. Each replayed prediction replaces its region in the otherwise detached canvas, and chunk mask restricts the update to that region. The scores retain full-sequence context, while gradients flow through the active prediction and its spatial interpolation, excluding other chunks and cached history. An auxiliary teacher target supports final-stage detail refinement. For sampled noninitial chunk, the frozen base model starts from the students lifted state, conditions on preceding final clean audiovisual chunks, and denoises to an endpoint. We regress the students final video prediction toward this target, complementing the joint audiovisual DMD objective. Training also includes speech-completion examples so the model learns when to stop speaking as well as how to continue. We select source clips whose endpoint is confirmed offline by the transcript, timestamped ASR, and voice activity detection [34], and extend the rollout beyond that endpoint. Here 𝐴 + 𝐵 is the full original transcript: the generator first receives 𝐴 + 𝐵, then its final span 𝐵, with no added 𝐶. Both scores receive the full transcript and an instruction to finish the unspoken remainder and then produce natural nonspeech behavior. Audio history indicates whether words remain to be spoken or the utterance has ended.

sections.title: 4 Experiments
sections.content: 4.1 Evaluation setup We evaluate long-form quality, isolate spatial-schedule efficiency, and measure gains from deployment and continuation training. Model and sequences. We train rank-128 LoRA on 10,000 self-constructed distillation pairs, starting from MiniMax-H3 FL2VA model [35]. We evaluate the methods on 100 self-constructed sequences lasting 110 minutes, each comprising successive five-second text requests. Outputs are 7681376 at 24 FPS with 32-kHz stereo audio. We also generate hour-long audiovisual streams by continuing the autoregressive rollout across successive text windows. Figure 1 shows samples at 1376 768, with frames sampled from the opening to 60 seconds to illustrate persistent character appearance and scene composition. Quality and efficiency metrics. Table 1 uses VABench VisualRealism, AudioAes, LipSync, and Desync for visual quality, audio quality, and audiovisual synchronization [41]. Temporal measures frame-difference stability, while Long-range measures color/brightness continuity across full sequences. CER compares Whisper-small transcripts [42] with the dialogue. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) summarize the short-time spectral envelope. We compare their mean-and-standard-deviation vectors over the first and last five seconds by cosine similarity to measure endpoint acoustic consistency. For the spatial ablation, Video averages normalized sharpness, contrast, exposure, and saturation, while Audio averages loudness, clipping, silence prevalence, and audiovisual-duration agreement. Efficiency is measured by GPUs per stream, generation FPS, and first ordered RGB latency. 4.2 Comparison with audio-video generators Table 1 organizes the comparison into audio-video foundation and accelerated clip models, speech-to-video (S2V) systems, and streaming audio-video generators. The first group comprises MiniMax-H3 [35], VDN [24], LTX2.3 [1], JavisDiT++ [2], MOVA [4], and OVI [3]. The S2V group comprises OmniAvatar [36], StableAvatar [37], Wan2.2-S2V [38], LiveAvatar [39], and Hallo3 [40], which animate video from supplied speech. The streaming group comprises OmniForcing [5], Lynn Standard/Flash [7], and TaoMate [6], which jointly generate speech and video across successive temporal blocks. The models extend generation through different forms of context. MiniMax-H3 and VDN extend an opening T2AV clip with successive I2AV clips. Lynn retains persistent media KV, while ours combines retained audiovisual history with overlapping dialogue and evolving scenes. MiniMax-H3 uses 49 denoising evaluations per five-second request, VDN uses eight, and the Lynn variants use four or three per autoregressive window. Our model uses three denoising evaluations and three clean-history encodings per chunk. Table 1 reports quality for both serial and parallel configurations. Figure 5 illustrates deviations from the intended text using TaoMate-HD and baseline training without asymmetric distillation. The displayed input windows identify the shared words retained when TaoMate-HD advances its text condition. The baseline repeats an upcoming clause or substitutes the intended sentence ending with words from the following sentence. 9 TaoMate-HD Technical Report October Figure 5. Thumbnail strips span each video, and colored intervals mark the transcribed excerpts. Its transcripts show repeated clause (left) and an incorrect sentence continuation (right). sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: We presented TaoMate-HD to reduce the computational cost of high-resolution audiovisual streaming while maintaining speech continuity. Progressive denoising establishes coarse video structure before final highresolution refinement, while stage-local KV history enables overlapping generation across chunks. Distillation with asymmetric text conditioning teaches the model to use retained audiovisual history as dialogue windows advance. Experiments show that progressive generation achieves 1.60 speedup over direct generation while retaining fine visual detail. The optimized stage-parallel deployment provides further 1.92 speedup. Asymmetric distillation reduces CER from 30.8% to 19.6%. Together, these advances support high-resolution audiovisual generation extending to an hour. 10 TaoMate-HD
